findings.issue: The history note is built as "Shipment cancelled by seller: " + reason (30-character prefix; the admin prefix at line 104 is 29). CancelOrder.reason only enforces @Size(max = 500), but order_status_history.note is varchar(500) and OrderStatusHistory.of does not truncate. Any reason of 471-500 characters (seller) or 472-500 (admin) is valid input yet makes T3 (OrderStore.commitCancel -> orders.flush()) fail with a value-too-long error. T3 runs after the strict card leg has already refunded under ship-cancel-<sid>. T3 then rolls back, which leaves the card money moved with refunded_amount not recorded, the wallet credit not queued, stock not released and the shipment stuck in REQUESTED, where it cannot be shipped (409). Replaying the same request fails the same way every time. Only a retry with a shorter reason recovers it (same key, so no double refund). Any approved seller can trigger this on their own shipments, and any admin on any shipment.
findings.fix: Make the note length safe before any money moves. Either cap the reason for these endpoints (for example a dedicated DTO with @Size(max = 450)) or truncate the note to 500 in OrderStatusHistory.of / Order.record. Also check the final note length in T1 (claimCancel) so a bad note is rejected before the card leg. Add a test with a 500-character reason on both endpoints.

findings.issue: cardLeg treats a PENDING card refund as accepted, and T3 records it as refunded. A PENDING that later settles FAILED leaves refunded_amount and PARTIALLY_REFUNDED/REFUNDED overstated while the customer has not been paid. This is disclosed in the design as a known gap (backlog item 4) with no settlement watch, unlike the return-refund poller.
findings.fix: Track the backlog item. Ideally store the card refund state on the shipment and reuse the return-refund settlement poller, or alert when a ship-cancel-* refund stays non-SUCCEEDED.

findings.issue: In PR-A alone, completesOrder, fullyRefunded and shippingAlreadyRefunded on the return path ignore cancelled shipments. A return made after a partial cancel therefore never carries shipping (customer under-refund), and fullyRefunded may never become true. This does not over-refund, because the cancel side computes shipping-once correctly, but the return side is only fixed in Part B.
findings.fix: Enforce CTO condition 1: do not merge PR-A without PR-B, and land them together.

findings.issue: The seller's free-text reason is stored as a history note and returned to the customer in the order timeline (OrderMapper TimelineEntryResponse). A seller can put arbitrary text (contact details, phishing) on the customer's order page. React escapes it, so there is no XSS. The seller /status note has the same exposure today.
findings.fix: Optionally store the seller reason only in an internal or admin field, or show the customer a fixed note (for example "Shipment cancelled by seller").

summary: Security review of PR-A a764802: authorization, double-refund protection, wallet keys, concurrency and logs all hold. One major: a valid reason of more than about 470 characters makes the history note longer than varchar(500), so T3 fails after the card refund has gone out, leaving the ledger wrong and the shipment stuck in REQUESTED. Minors: the disclosed PENDING-then-FAILED gap, PR-A must merge with PR-B, and seller free text in the customer timeline. (Full summary in the session transcript.)
